hero.headline: Agentic AI workflows for data-driven restaurant marketing
hero.subtitle: Upload sales data, explore analytics-backed signals, then run workflow milestones that produce structured outputs—schedules, angles, and copy—through agentic pipelines, chat, and reusable artifacts.

landing.problem: Most restaurant marketing still runs on spreadsheets, static playbooks, and gut feel—without agentic automation that turns live sales data into repeatable workflow outputs. Teams miss demand signals, burn budget on the wrong promos, and never get from insight to publish-ready assets in one system.
landing.problemImageAlt: Abstract analytics dashboard showing sales performance bars and insight summary.
landing.solution: Menuyukti is built as a workflow platform: workflows are sequences of milestones that fetch context, run AI steps (LangGraph-style agent service), and persist structured milestone data—not only chat. Your flagship use case is restaurant marketing: sales and menu signals feed those workflows so you get Instagram-oriented schedules and content you can refine in the app and reuse across locations.
landing.solutionImageAlt: Workflow diagram from POS data through AI milestones to stored workflow outputs and artifacts.

trust.stat1Label: Workflows with steps that ingest data, run models, and save outputs for what comes next.
trust.stat2Label: Web app, GraphQL API, and Python agent service share the same workspace data—analytics plus agents.
trust.stat3Label: Chat to steer work; review and edit generated captions, ideas, and plans as reusable assets.

bento.title: Analytics, agents, and deliverables together
bento.subtitle: The product focuses on composable pipelines: structured data in, milestone results out—grounded in how your locations actually perform.
bento.item1Description: Insights computed from uploaded POS or spreadsheet reports—what sells, mix shifts, and patterns worth promoting before you brief creative.
bento.item2Description: Prepare and run workflow steps with LLM-backed graphs: plan-and-execute style flows, reflection where drafts are critiqued and revised, and outputs written back as milestone data.
bento.item3Description: Steer agents in conversation, iterate on drafts, and keep schedules and copy as artifacts you can revisit—not a one-off thread that disappears.

faq.title: Common questions
faq.q1: What data do I need to upload?
faq.a1: Typical POS or spreadsheet exports work—sales by item, category, or ticket over time. The GraphQL-backed workspace stores what you import so analytics and agents can use the same source of truth.
faq.q2: Is my sales data shared with third parties?
faq.a2: Your data powers your workspace and insights. We do not sell your data. Details are covered in our privacy policy.
faq.a3: Chat is how you collaborate, but the core model is workflows: ordered milestones that produce stored, structured outputs—schedules, profiles, evaluations—not only messages. Agents call platform APIs when they need your data.
faq.a4: Restaurant marketers, in-house creatives, and agencies running multi-location brands who want analytics plus agentic automation in one place—not disconnected dashboards and ad hoc prompts.
faq.a5: Yes—work across locations, workflows, milestones, and brand assets as your organization scales.

pdp.accordionShippingBody: Each order is printed after checkout—allow 3–5 business days for production plus transit time. Tracking is sent when your package leaves our partner lab. International delivery may incur duties.
pdp.accordionReturnsBody: Because pieces are made to order, returns are limited to damage in transit or print defects—contact us within 14 days with photos of the packaging and item. Color variation up to 10% versus your screen is normal for giclée and canvas.
pdp.accordionCareBody: Handle framed and canvas works with clean, dry hands. Dust lightly with a soft microfiber cloth; avoid household cleaners on the print surface. Keep out of direct sunlight to preserve color for years in hospitality environments.

agents.title: Agents
agents.description: Marketing agents that transform sales data into actionable insights.

items.top_items: The menu items with the highest demand or strongest performance in the selected analysis context.
items.peak_hours: The hourly windows where demand is highest and audience attention is most concentrated.
items.weekday_bias: A directional signal showing whether demand is stronger on weekdays or weekends.
items.daypart_demand_distribution: Relative demand split across dayparts (morning, lunch, afternoon, evening).
items.weekday_demand_distribution: Relative demand split across days of the week.
items.audience_intent_clusters: Behavior-based groupings of customer intent inferred from ordering patterns.
items.party_size_signal: A derived indicator of likely order context (solo, pair, or group) from basket behavior.
items.social_dining_probability: An estimate of how likely orders are associated with shared or social consumption.
items.audience_mix_summary: A concise summary of dominant audience behavior segments in the selected dataset.
items.analysis_window: The effective time range of data used to compute the audience outputs.
items.popularity_index_summary: A summary of item popularity scores used to detect preference concentration.
items.top_item_revenue_share: The share of total revenue contributed by top-performing menu items.
items.category_mix: The relative demand or revenue contribution of each menu category.
items.tone_profile: The overall voice and personality to apply across Instagram posts and reels.
items.language_guidelines: Rules for language choice, tone, and readability for your audience.
items.caption_style: Recommended structure and style for Instagram captions.
items.hashtag_style: Guidelines for hashtag selection, volume, and mix.
items.content_dos_donts: Content do's and don'ts to keep posts on-brand and effective.
items.post_concepts: Short concepts or themes to shape upcoming Instagram posts.
items.cta_phrases: Suggested call-to-action phrases aligned with the audience.
items.emoji_guidelines: Emoji usage guidance to match tone without overusing.

chat.milestone1PassCriteria:
Trade area and peak hours are documented with sources or assumptions called out.
Guest segments are named with at least one supporting signal (sales, reviews, or staff input).
Site positioning, hero menu items, and hard constraints (hours, brand, compliance) are explicit.
Profile is factual enough for downstream audience and offer recommendations.
chat.milestone1Input: Paste notes from your GM or link to your last menu refresh…
chat.milestone1ResultMarkdown:
## Location profile (draft)

**Trade area:** 12–15 min drive around the site; lunch office crowd Tue–Thu.

**Segments:** power lunch (35%), families weekend (28%), delivery dinner (22%).

**Constraints:** kitchen closes 9:30pm; no alcohol promos without manager approval.
chat.milestone2PassCriteria:
Objectives are measurable (reach, visits, or revenue) and time-bound.
Primary audience ties back to the location profile segments.
!Primary audience is still too broad — narrow to one segment (example not met).
?Key messages, channels, and timing fit the brand and local context (pending validation).
?Budget split and channel mix under review (pending).
?Stakeholders who must approve are listed or implied (pending confirmation).
chat.milestone2Input: Optional: objectives, promos already approved, dates to avoid…
chat.milestone2ResultMarkdown:
## Workflow brief

**Goal:** lift weekday lunch covers by 8% over 4 weeks.

**Audience:** office workers within 10 minutes, Tue–Thu 11:30–1:30.

**Messages:** speed of service, chef’s lunch set, loyalty nudge.

**Channels:** Instagram feed + Stories; in-store QR to follow.
